claims.text: The kind filter is what actually keeps a type node out of the file world; this is defence in depth, and it makes a leak legible in a diff instead of only in a stack trace.

claims.text: The two node kinds that are NOT files.  Kept as a literal here rather than imported from typegraph so this module stays a pure normaliser of an index dict with no dependency on the producer of one of its blocks -- the same reason document is a string literal below and not an import from markdown.  dss.FILE_NODE_KINDS is the set these are held OUT of; see this module's docstring for why that is arithmetic and not taste.
claims.why: References to typegraph, markdown, dss.FILE_NODE_KINDS, and module docstring are outside this chunk.

claims.text: index["type_edges"] is a mapping keyed by relation name, and this module publishes whatever keys it finds -- a seventh relation (instantiates is the planned one) then needs no edit here.  What it may NOT do is land in a layer that already means something else: an edge with a type endpoint filed under imports would be read as an import by every consumer of that layer, starting with the reachability the safety fence is built on.  Refuse rather than merge.
claims.why: References to index["type_edges"], layer semantics, and safety fence are outside this chunk.
